standard_prerequisites.name: Free Schrödinger evolution
standard_prerequisites.statement: Q_FS(t) = e^{i hbar t Delta / 2} Q_in e^{-i hbar t Delta / 2} is the solution of the free Schrödinger equation.
standard_prerequisites.use: It defines the density whose Fourier modes are estimated, and its equation is retained as context.

standard_prerequisites.name: Commutation of the quantum operators
standard_prerequisites.statement: The quantum derivatives and position operators commute in the four combinations recorded in the author's remark.
standard_prerequisites.use: It allows the identities for the individual operators to be extended to the joint weight at source line 557.

standard_prerequisites.name: Weighted Sobolev norm H^{N0}_{M,M}
standard_prerequisites.statement: The norm controls the kernel up to order N0 in both variables with the weight M = ceil((d+1)/2).
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the norm on the right-hand side of the estimate.

core_obligations: Recall the identity for the Fourier transform of the density, namely that it equals the Wigner transform of Q_in evaluated at (k, kt) (source line 557).

Use the commutation remark to extend the identities for the individual quantum operators to the joint weight <nabla_x, nabla_xi>^{N0}, and rewrite the weighted Fourier transform as the Fourier transform of the Wigner transform of the weighted initial datum (source lines 557-560).

Apply the retained identity for the Fourier transform of the Wigner transform to bound the result by the weighted Sobolev norm of Q_in divided by <k, kt>^{N0}, which is the stated decay (source line 561).

proof_roadmap.step: Identify the Fourier transform of the density and invoke commutation to extend the operator identities to the joint weight.
Rewrite the weighted mode as a Wigner transform of a weighted datum.
Apply the Fourier-transform identity for the Wigner transform and read off the bound.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled proposition `propfreephasemixing` at source lines 550-555: for every t >= 0 and every frequency k, the Fourier mode of the density of the free Schrödinger solution decays like the weighted Sobolev norm of the initial datum divided by <k, kt>^{N0}. The author's proof (source lines 556-562) is short but it is a composite of three separate inputs that have to be combined in the right order: the Fourier representation of the density (line 557), the commutation remark which is what allows the identities for the individual quantum operators to be promoted to the joint weight <nabla_x, nabla_xi>^{N0} (line 557), and the identity for the Fourier transform of the Wigner transform, which is applied only after the weighted mode has been rewritten as a Wigner transform of a weighted initial datum (lines 559-561). The statement mentions only the decay estimate and the norm on the right-hand side.
